Archive item 1: Marlowe & Vine Press Manual 2023
Source format: Maintenance manual

**1.1 Purpose**
This manual provides operating and maintenance instructions for Press No. 3, a web offset printing press manufactured for the Marlowe & Vine Group. The manual is intended for use by trained press operators, maintenance technicians, and shift supervisors. All personnel must read and understand the relevant sections before operating or servicing the press.

**1.2 Safety Warnings**
- **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Always isolate the main electrical supply and pneumatic supply before performing any maintenance or cleaning task that requires access to moving parts. Use the assigned lock and tag. Only the person who applied the lock may remove it.
- **Nip Points:** The press contains multiple in-running nips. Keep hands, loose clothing, and tools clear of all nips. Guards must be in place at all times except during approved maintenance.
- **Hot Surfaces:** Dryer and chill roll sections operate at high temperatures. Allow components to cool for at least 15 minutes after shutdown before accessing them.
- **Chemical Safety:** Blanket washes and solvents are flammable. Use only in well-ventilated areas. No smoking or open flames in the press hall. Refer to SDS sheets in the control room.
- **Noise:** Sound levels may exceed 85 dBA during operation. Wear hearing protection when in the press hall.
- **Lifting:** Use approved lifting points only. Never lift the press or its major components by hand. Use the overhead crane for units heavier than 50 kg.
- **Emergency Stop:** The press is equipped with emergency stop (E-stop) buttons at each unit and at the main control console. Pressing any E-stop will immediately halt the press drive and close the pneumatic line. Restart requires a full reset procedure (see Section 4.8).
- **Electrical Safety:** Only qualified electricians may open electrical enclosures. Capacitors may retain a charge; discharge as per Section 11.3.

**1.3 Training Requirement**
Only personnel who have completed the Marlowe & Vine Press Operator Training Program and have been signed off on Press No. 3 are authorized to operate the press. A list of authorised operators is maintained on the noticeboard outside the press hall.

---

**2. General Specifications**

**2.1 Press Configuration**
Press No. 3 is a four-unit, heat-set web offset press with a 578 mm web width and a 620 mm cut-off. It is configured for two-side printing on coated and uncoated papers. The press is fitted with an in-line folder and a sheeter.

**2.2 Speed Rating**
The manual states that Press No. 3 has press speed rating 45000 copies per hour. Record status: current. This rating is based on a standard 16-page signature (broadsheet) at a basis weight of 50 gsm. Speed is measured at the folder delivery. The press may be operated at speeds up to this rating, but running at maximum speed for extended periods may increase wear on the blanket cylinders and paper dust build-up in the folder. For running speed recommendations based on stock, refer to Section 4.4.

**2.3 Dimensional and Weight Data (Approximate)**

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Overall Length (infeed to folder) | 22.4 m |
| Overall Width (including console) | 4.8 m |
| Height to top of dryer | 3.1 m |
| Total Weight (dry) | 38,500 kg |
| Max Paper Roll Diameter | 1.25 m |
| Max Paper Roll Width | 590 mm |

**2.4 Electrical Supply**
- Main Supply: 400V, 3-phase, 50Hz
- Control Voltage: 24V DC
- Total Installed Load: 185 kW (excluding dryer)
- Dryer Load: 95 kW

**2.5 Pneumatic Supply**
- Required Pressure: 6.5 bar (max 8 bar)
- Air Quality: Filtered to 5 microns, dried to a dew point of +3°C
- Consumption: 12 m³/hr at full speed

**2.6 Water Supply (Chill Roll System)**
- Inlet Temperature: 10-12°C
- Flow Rate: 80 L/min per chill roll stand
- Water Quality: Treated, pH 7.0-8.5
**Table 3.1 – Recommended Web Tensions (N/m of web width)**

| Stock Type | Basis Weight (gsm) | Tension (N/m) |
|------------|--------------------|---------------|
| Newsprint   | 40–45             | 350           |
| Uncoated    | 50–60             | 420           |
| Coated      | 60–70             | 480           |
| Coated      | 70–80             | 520           |

These values are for a single web. If running a double-web configuration, add 15% to the total tension setting. Tension should be checked at the beginning of each shift and after any change of reel. The tension readout on the console shows the value at the infeed nip.

Note: The tension values above were revised in the 2023 update. The previous edition of this manual (2019) listed values approximately 10% lower, based on the older dancer-roll control system. The new values reflect the upgraded load-cell system installed in early 2022. If any part of the press still uses the older dancer-roll settings, refer to the archived Section 3.3 in the 2019 manual held in the maintenance office.

**3.4 Web Guides**

Two web guides are fitted: one at the infeed and one ahead of the folder. Each guide uses an infra-red edge sensor to keep the web laterally aligned. The guide rollers are pneumatically positioned.

- Guide response time: 0.2 seconds (nominal)
- Maximum lateral correction: ±15 mm
- Air supply to guides: 6.5 bar, as per Section 2.5

If a guide oscillates or fails to hold position, check the sensor lens for paper dust. Clean with a soft, dry cloth only. Do not use solvent. If the guide continues to hunt, check the air pressure at the guide manifold and the condition of the guide rollers for wear.

**3.5 Web Break Detectors**

Web break detectors are located:

- After the infeed unit
- After each printing unit
- After the chill roll stands
- At the folder inlet

According to the manual, Press No. 3 has web width 1.4 metres. Record status: current.

The detectors are contact-type, using a low-voltage sensing bar. When a break is detected, the press stops automatically and the detector location is shown on the console display. The web break detector sensitivity should be checked weekly. Adjust the sensitivity so that a light finger press on the sensing bar triggers a stop, but normal web flutter does not.

**3.6 Chill Roll Stands**

There are two chill roll stands, each with three rolls. The chill roll system is supplied with treated water at 10–12°C and a flow rate of 80 L/min per stand, as per Section 2.6. The water temperature is controlled by the chiller unit located outside the press hall.

Web tension through the chill roll stands should be maintained at the same value as the infeed tension. If the web is over-tensioned through the chill rolls, it can cause ink picking on coated stocks. If under-tensioned, the web can bag and cause wrinkles at the folder.

**3.7 Folder Infeed Tension**

The folder infeed has its own nip roll set. Tension here should be slightly lower than the main web tension – approximately 90% of the value in Table 3.1. This prevents web pull at the folder former. The folder nip pressure is set hydraulically and should be checked during the weekly preventive maintenance routine.

**3.8 Dryer**

The dryer is a hot-air, gas-fired unit. The dryer temperature profile is set by the operator according to the ink coverage and stock type. Typical settings are given in Section 4.4. The dryer has an automatic web break shutdown that isolates the gas supply if a web break occurs while the press is running.

**4. Printing Units**

**4.1 Unit Configuration**

Press No. 3 has four printing units, each configured for one colour. The units are numbered from the infeed side: Unit 1 (black), Unit 2 (cyan), Unit 3 (magenta), Unit 4 (yellow). Each unit has a blanket cylinder, plate cylinder, and impression cylinder arrangement.
The dryer temperature profile should be set according to the ink coverage and stock type. The following table gives typical settings. These are starting points only; the operator should adjust them based on the actual print result.

| Stock Type          | Ink Coverage | Dryer Temperature (°C) |
|---------------------|--------------|------------------------|
| Newsprint           | Light        | 90–100                 |
| Newsprint           | Heavy        | 110–120                |
| Coated stock        | Light        | 100–110                |
| Coated stock        | Heavy        | 120–130                |

If the dryer temperature is set too high, the web can blister or curl. If set too low, the ink will not dry properly and can mark or set off on the folder.

**4.5 Ink Viscosity Specifications**

The ink viscosity should be maintained within the following ranges. Viscosity is measured using the standard flow cup supplied with the press. The measurement should be taken at the unit, not at the bulk supply tank, because the viscosity can change as the ink travels through the pipework.

| Ink Colour | Viscosity Range (seconds) |
|------------|---------------------------|
| Black      | 25–30                     |
| Cyan       | 28–32                     |
| Magenta    | 28–32                     |
| Yellow     | 30–35                     |

**4.6 Plate Cylinder and Blanket Cylinder**

The plate cylinder has a single plate lockup. The plate is clamped at the leading edge and tensioned at the trailing edge. When fitting a new plate, the trailing edge should be pulled tight to prevent the plate from working loose during the run. The plate cylinder bearer rings should be checked for wear during the monthly maintenance routine. If the bearers are worn, the plate can bounce and cause a visible band across the print.

The manual lists Press No. 3 has oil filter part number MV-3456-01. Record status: current.

The blanket cylinder is fitted with a compressible blanket. The blanket should be replaced when the print quality deteriorates, typically after 500,000 impressions. The blanket should be cleaned with the automatic blanket wash system at the end of each shift. The blanket wash system uses a solvent which is supplied from the central solvent supply.

The blanket cylinder bearer rings should be checked for wear at the same time as the plate cylinder bearers. If the bearers are worn, the nip pressure will be uneven, and this can cause a ghosting effect in the print.

**4.7 Impression Cylinder**

The impression cylinder is not fitted with a blanket. The impression cylinder provides the backing for the web as it passes through the nip. The impression cylinder surface should be kept clean and free from ink build-up. If ink builds up on the impression cylinder, it can transfer to the back of the web and cause marking in the next unit.

**5. Ancillary Equipment**

**5.1 Oil Lubrication System**

Press No. 3 is fitted with a centralised oil lubrication system. The system supplies oil to the main bearings, the gearboxes, and the folders. The oil is pumped from a reservoir located in the basement below the press hall. The oil level in the reservoir should be checked daily, and the oil should be topped up if the level is below the minimum mark on the sight glass.

The oil lubrication system has a filter which should be replaced every 6 months. The filter is a spin-on type. The part number for the oil filter for Press No. 3 is MV-3456-01. This part number is current and should be used when ordering replacements. The oil filter is located on the side of the oil reservoir, and it is accessible from the walkway at the infeed end of the press. Record status: current.
The system pressure should be maintained between 2.0 and 2.5 bar. The pressure is set by the pressure-reducing valve on the make-up water line. If the pressure drops below 1.5 bar, the low-pressure switch will stop the press. The make-up water is supplied from the mains via a float valve in the header tank. The header tank is located on the roof above the press hall.

The water filters are bag-type filters. They should be replaced when the differential pressure across the filter reaches 1.0 bar. The differential pressure is shown on the gauge on the filter housing. The part number for the water filter bags is MV-2210-BAG. Record status: current.

**5.3 Ancillary Pumps**

The press hall is served by several ancillary pumps. These pumps are used for the oil lubrication system, the water circulation system, and the solvent supply system. The pumps are not part of the main press drive.

The pumps are grouped together in the pump room, which is located at the basement level below the press hall. The pump room is accessed via the stairs at the reelstand end of the press. The pump room is also used for storage of maintenance materials. Do not store rags or solvent-soaked waste in the pump room. They must be kept in the designated fire-proof bins outside the pump room.

Each pump has a nameplate attached to the motor. The nameplate shows the pump type, the serial number, and the date of manufacture. The serial number should be quoted on all parts orders and in the maintenance log.

**5.4 Ancillary Pump 7**

Ancillary Pump 7 is located at the far end of the pump room, next to the oil reservoir. The manual specifies Ancillary Pump 7 has pump type centrifugal. Record status: current.

Ancillary Pump 7 is used for the transfer of oil from the bulk storage tank to the oil reservoir. The bulk storage tank is located outside the pump room, against the basement wall. The pump is not used for the main oil circulation loop.

The pump is a close-coupled centrifugal pump. The pump is driven by a 5.5 kW electric motor. The motor is a three-phase, 415 V, 50 Hz unit. The motor is fitted with a thermal overload relay which is set to the motor full-load current. The overload relay is located in the motor starter panel, which is mounted on the wall adjacent to the pump.

The pump discharge pressure should be checked when the pump is running. The normal discharge pressure is between 3.0 and 4.0 bar. The discharge pressure is shown on the gauge on the discharge pipework. The gauge is a glycerine-filled type. The pump suction pressure is not normally monitored. If the suction strainer becomes blocked, the pump will cavitate. Cavitation can be heard as a rattling or knocking noise from the pump.

The pump is fitted with a mechanical seal. The mechanical seal requires no routine maintenance. The seal should be inspected for leaks during the monthly visual inspection. If the seal leaks, the pump must be taken out of service and the seal replaced. The seal kit part number is MV-2210-SEAL.

**5.4.1 Ancillary Pump 7 Installation Notes**

The pump is mounted on a concrete plinth. The plinth is raised 150 mm above the pump room floor. The pump is secured to the plinth with four M16 foundation bolts. The foundation bolts are grouted into the plinth. The pump alignment should be checked after any work on the foundation bolts.

The suction pipework is 80 mm nominal bore. The discharge pipework is 50 mm nominal bore. The discharge pipework rises vertically from the pump and then runs along the wall to the oil reservoir. The discharge pipework is fitted with a non-return valve. The non-return valve is located immediately after the discharge gate valve. The discharge gate valve is used to isolate the pump for maintenance.
| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Rated flow | 120 L/min | At duty point, see curve below |
| Normal discharge pressure | 3.0 – 4.0 bar | See Section 5.4 |
| Maximum discharge pressure | 5.5 bar | At shut-off, do not run against closed gate valve for more than 2 minutes |
| Minimum suction pressure | 0.3 bar absolute | At pump suction flange |
| Motor rating | 5.5 kW | See Section 5.4 |
| Motor full-load current | 10.6 A | At 415 V, 50 Hz |
| Pump speed | 1450 rpm | Direct drive, close-coupled |
| Maximum oil temperature | 60 °C | At pump suction |
| Minimum oil temperature | 10 °C | For start-up, see Section 5.4.3 |
| NPSH required | 2.1 m | At rated flow, cold water equivalent |

**5.4.2.1 Performance Curve**

The performance curve for Ancillary Pump 7 is reproduced in Drawing MV-AP7-PC-001,
which is held in the drawing register in the maintenance office. A reduced-size copy is
mounted on the wall inside the pump room, next to the motor starter panel. The curve
shows the relationship between flow and discharge head for the pump at 1450 rpm.

The curve is based on the works test and has been verified on site. Site verification
was carried out using the temporary flow meter that is kept in the stores. The
temporary flow meter is a clamp-on ultrasonic type. It is not permanently installed.
The meter is suitable for flow measurement on the 50 mm discharge pipework.

Three points from the curve are reproduced below for quick reference. These are the
points most often used when checking pump performance.

**Table 5.4.2.2 – Performance Curve Reference Points**

| Flow (L/min) | Discharge Head (m) | Equivalent Pressure (bar) | Notes |
|--------------|--------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| 60 | 34.5 | 3.4 | Low flow, high head |
| 120 | 31.0 | 3.0 | Duty point |
| 160 | 24.5 | 2.4 | High flow, low head |

The manual indicates Ancillary Pump 7 has rated flow 120 litres per minute. Record status: current.

The discharge head is measured in metres of liquid column. The equivalent pressure is
given in bar for convenience, and assumes the oil specific gravity is 0.88. If a
different oil is used, the pressure gauge reading will change even though the pump is
operating at the same point on the curve. Do not use the pressure gauge reading to
infer flow unless the oil specific gravity is known.

**5.4.2.2 Effect of Oil Viscosity**

The performance data given in Section 5.4.2.1 is for oil with a viscosity of 32 cSt at
40 °C. This is the standard oil used in the press lubrication system. If a higher
viscosity oil is used, the pump flow will be reduced at the same discharge pressure.
The motor current will also increase.

For oil with a viscosity of 46 cSt at 40 °C, the flow at the duty point is reduced by
approximately 8%. This should be taken into account when estimating reservoir fill
time. If a viscosity of 68 cSt is used, the flow reduction is approximately 15%. The
pump is not suitable for oils with a viscosity above 68 cSt without consultation with
the pump manufacturer.

The viscosity of the oil in use should be checked when investigating any apparent
reduction in pump flow. The oil viscosity is normally stated on the oil delivery
certificate. A simple check is to compare the oil temperature at the pump suction with
the expected temperature for the current operating conditions. If the oil is cooler
than normal, the viscosity will be higher and the flow will be lower.

**5.4.2.3 Flow Measurement Methods**

There is no permanently installed flow meter on the Ancillary Pump 7 discharge
pipework. Flow is inferred from the discharge pressure gauge and the performance
curve. This is sufficient for routine checks. For more accurate measurement, the
temporary flow meter can be fitted to the discharge pipework.
The flow meter should be installed on a straight run of pipe, with at least five
pipe diameters of straight pipe upstream and two pipe diameters downstream of the
meter. This reduces the effect of flow disturbances on the reading. For the
Ancillary Pump 7 discharge pipework, the boss is located approximately 300 mm
downstream of the pump flange, which is within an acceptable straight run.

**5.4.2.5 Pressure Gauge Check**

The discharge pressure gauge is a 0-10 bar gauge with a 63 mm dial. The gauge is
wetted with glycerine to damp vibration. Check the gauge glass for cracks or
clouding at each routine inspection. A cloudy glass can make the reading difficult
to see and should be replaced.

The gauge should read zero when the pump is stopped and the discharge valve is
closed. If the gauge does not return to zero, the gauge is faulty or the pressure
sensing line is blocked. The pressure sensing line is a 6 mm OD stainless steel
tube. It should be purged if there is any doubt about the reading. Do not rely on
a faulty gauge reading to set the pump duty point.

**5.4.3 Ancillary Pump 7 – Maintenance Schedule**

Ancillary Pump 7 is subject to a scheduled maintenance programme. The schedule is
based on operating hours, which are recorded on the pump hour meter. The hour
meter is located on the pump control panel, next to the start/stop buttons. The
reading should be recorded at the end of each shift in the Press Room Shift Log.

The manual states Ancillary Pump 7 has maintenance interval 500 operating hours. Record status: current.
This interval is current for all maintenance tasks listed in Table 5.4.3.1. The
interval is measured in operating hours, not calendar time. A pump that runs
continuously will require maintenance more frequently than a pump that runs
intermittently. Record the hour meter reading at each maintenance event and
calculate the next due date based on the expected running hours per week.

**Table 5.4.3.1 – Ancillary Pump 7 Maintenance Tasks**

| Item | Task Description | Interval (hours) | Notes |
|------|------------------|------------------|-------|
| 1 | Check oil level in bearing housing | 500 | Top up with ISO VG 32 if required |
| 2 | Check coupling alignment | 500 | Use dial indicator; max 0.1 mm |
| 3 | Check coupling element for wear | 500 | Replace if cracks or missing rubber |
| 4 | Check mechanical seal for leakage | 500 | Minor weep is acceptable; drip must be investigated |
| 5 | Check suction strainer for debris | 500 | Clean if pressure drop exceeds 0.3 bar |
| 6 | Check discharge pressure at duty point | 500 | Compare with Section 5.4.2.1 |
| 7 | Check motor current at duty point | 500 | Compare with nameplate FLA |
| 8 | Check pump vibration | 500 | Use handheld vibrometer; max 4.5 mm/s RMS |
| 9 | Check bearing temperature | 500 | Max 80 °C at bearing housing |
| 10 | Check for unusual noise | 500 | Report any change in tone or level |
| 11 | Check all pipework joints for leaks | 500 | Tighten or remake as required |
| 12 | Check baseplate bolts for tightness | 500 | Torque to 80 Nm |

The maintenance tasks listed in Table 5.4.3.1 are to be carried out at each
500 operating hour interval. The tasks should be completed by a competent
maintenance technician. After completion, the technician should sign and date the
Maintenance Record Sheet (Form MV-214) and enter the hour meter reading in the
appropriate column.

**5.4.3.1 Oil Change**

The oil in the bearing housing should be changed at every second maintenance
interval, i.e. at 1000 operating hours. The oil specification is ISO VG 32 mineral
oil. Drain the oil while the pump is warm, but not running. Remove the drain plug
at the bottom of the bearing housing and allow the oil to drain into a suitable
container. Dispose of the used oil in accordance with site procedures. Refit the
drain plug and fill with new oil to the level indicated on the sight glass. The
oil level should be at the centre of the sight glass when the pump is stopped.

| Item | Part Number | Description | Quantity |
|------|-------------|-------------|----------|
| 1 | MV-P2001 | Mechanical seal kit | 1 |
| 2 | MV-P2002 | Bearing housing gasket | 2 |
| 3 | MV-P2003 | Coupling element | 1 |
| 4 | MV-P2004 | Suction strainer element | 1 |
| 5 | MV-P2005 | Pressure switch | 1 |
| 6 | MV-P2006 | Oil sight glass | 1 |

**5.5 Backup Generator Set B**

Backup Generator Set B (BGS-B) provides standby electrical power to the press line
and ancillary equipment in the event of a mains supply failure. This section covers
the routine maintenance and operational checks for BGS-B. The generator is located in
the external generator compound adjacent to the press hall.

**5.5.1 General Description**

BGS-B is a diesel engine driven generator set. The engine is a six cylinder,
turbocharged diesel engine. The generator is a brushless alternator. The set is
mounted on a skid base with anti-vibration mounts. The generator set is designed for
standby duty and is not intended for continuous operation.

**5.5.2 Fuel System**

The fuel system consists of a day tank, a transfer pump, a fuel filter, and the
engine fuel injection system. The day tank is mounted on the skid base. Fuel is
supplied to the day tank from the main bulk fuel storage tank by the transfer pump.
The transfer pump is controlled by a level switch in the day tank. The fuel filter
should be changed at the intervals given in the maintenance schedule.

**5.5.2.1 Fuel Capacity**

The manual notes Backup Generator Set B has fuel capacity 800 litres. Record status: current. This is the
capacity of the day tank. The day tank is calibrated and a sight glass is fitted to
indicate the fuel level. The fuel level should be checked before each test run and
after any period of operation. If the fuel level is low, the day tank should be
topped up from the bulk storage tank using the transfer pump. The transfer pump
should be operated manually only when the generator is shut down.

**5.5.2.2 Fuel Quality**

The fuel used in BGS-B should be diesel fuel meeting the requirements of BS EN 590.
The fuel should be clean and free from water and sediment. Water in the fuel can
cause damage to the injection system. The fuel filter has a water separator element.
The water separator bowl should be drained at each maintenance interval. If the fuel
is suspected of being contaminated, a sample should be taken and tested. The bulk
fuel storage tank should be checked for water at regular intervals.

**5.5.3 Cooling System**

The engine is cooled by a radiator and fan. The cooling system is filled with a
mixture of water and antifreeze. The antifreeze concentration should be checked
before the winter period and adjusted to give protection to -20 °C. The coolant
level should be checked at each maintenance interval. The radiator fins should be
checked for blockage and cleaned with compressed air if necessary.

**5.5.4 Electrical System**

The generator set is controlled by an automatic mains failure (AMF) control panel.
The panel monitors the mains supply and initiates a start sequence for the generator
when a mains failure is detected. The panel also monitors the generator output and
provides protection against overload, short circuit, and low oil pressure. The
control panel is located in a weatherproof enclosure on the skid base.

**5.5.4.1 Control Panel Checks**

The following checks should be carried out on the control panel at each maintenance
interval:

1.  Check the panel for signs of moisture ingress or condensation.
2.  Check all indicator lamps and the digital display for correct operation.
3.  Check the battery charger for correct output voltage.
4.  Check the battery condition and electrolyte level.
5.  Check the emergency stop button for correct operation. Do not test the emergency
    stop with the generator running unless the procedure in Section 5.5.6 is being
    followed.
# 6. CONTROL SYSTEMS

## 6.1 Web Tension Controller (WTC)

The Web Tension Controller (WTC) is fitted to the main reel stand and provides closed-loop control of web tension between the unwind and the first printing unit. The controller maintains a set tension by adjusting the brake torque on the unwind shaft in response to signals from the load cells mounted on the dancer roller assembly.

The WTC is a microprocessor-based unit housed in a sheet-steel enclosure mounted on the side frame of the reel stand. The front panel comprises a backlit LCD display, a keypad for data entry, and indicator lamps for power, fault, and brake status. All operator adjustments are made via the keypad; no internal potentiometer adjustments are required for normal operation.

### 6.1.1 Technical Specifications

| Parameter | Specification |
|---|---|
| Supply voltage | 24 V DC nominal (20–30 V DC) |
| Power consumption | 12 W maximum |
| Display | 2-line × 16-character backlit LCD |
| Load cell input | 2 × 2 mV/V, 350 Ω bridge |
| Brake output | 0–24 V DC PWM, 3 A maximum |
| Analogue outputs | 0–10 V DC, 4–20 mA (isolated) |
| Serial interface | RS-485, Modbus RTU |
| Operating temperature | 0–50 °C |
| Enclosure rating | IP54 |

### 6.1.2 Firmware

The WTC is supplied with firmware version 3.2.1. The manual records Web Tension Controller has firmware version 3.2.1. Record status: current. This is the current production version and supersedes all earlier versions. The firmware version is shown on the display for approximately 5 seconds when power is applied to the unit.

Do not attempt to update the firmware in the field. Firmware updates are carried out by the manufacturer or by authorised service personnel only. The update procedure requires the use of a proprietary programming lead, which is not supplied with the machine. If the firmware version is not as stated above, contact Marlowe & Vine Group Service Department before placing the machine back into service.

### 6.1.3 Functional Description

The WTC receives signals from the two load cells mounted on the dancer roller. The load cells produce a small voltage proportional to the force applied by the web. The controller sums the two signals and compares the result with the set tension value entered by the operator. The difference between the actual and set tension produces an error signal, which is used to adjust the brake current.

The brake is a permanent-magnet particle brake. The controller supplies a pulse-width-modulated voltage to the brake coil. The duty cycle of the PWM signal determines the brake torque. The controller also provides a soft-start function to prevent web breakage on start-up.

The WTC has the following operating modes:

1. **Manual mode** — the operator sets the brake current directly as a percentage of full scale. The load cell feedback is ignored. This mode is used for initial set-up and for troubleshooting.
2. **Automatic mode** — the controller maintains the set tension using load cell feedback. This is the normal operating mode.
3. **Calibration mode** — used to zero the load cells and to set the full-scale calibration. Access to this mode requires a four-digit code, which is given in Section 6.1.6.

## 6.2 WTC Operator Controls

### 6.2.1 Front Panel

The front panel is arranged as follows:

- **Power lamp** — illuminated when 24 V DC is present.
- **Fault lamp** — illuminated when a fault condition is detected. The display shows the fault code (see Section 6.4).
- **Brake lamp** — illuminated when the brake is being energised.
- **Display** — two lines of 16 characters. Shows tension in kg, brake current as a percentage, and fault codes.
- **Keypad** — six keys: UP, DOWN, ENTER, ESC, MAN/AUTO, and CAL.
### 6.2.2 Keypad Functions

The six keys on the front panel have the following functions:

| Key | Function |
|------|-----------|
| UP / DOWN | Scroll through menu items, adjust values, and select fault code display. |
| ENTER | Confirm a selection or store a value. |
| ESC | Return to the previous menu level without storing changes. |
| MAN/AUTO | Toggle between Manual and Automatic mode. When the machine is running, the mode change takes effect immediately. |
| CAL | Enter Calibration mode. This key is only active when the machine is in Manual mode and the four-digit access code has been entered. |

**Note:** The MAN/AUTO key is ignored when the web is in motion. The controller will not accept a mode change while the press is running at speeds above 50 m/min. If the operator attempts to change mode at speed, the key press is ignored and the display shows `MODE LOCKED` for three seconds.

### 6.2.3 Menu Structure

The WTC has a two-level menu structure. The top level is selected by pressing the UP or DOWN keys when the display shows the running values. The second level is entered by pressing ENTER.

The menu items are as follows:

1. **SET TENSION** — sets the target tension in kg. Range: 0.0 to 50.0 kg.
2. **CAL ZERO** — zeroes the load cell output. See Section 6.1.6.
3. **CAL SPAN** — sets the full-scale calibration. See Section 6.1.6.
4. **BRAKE TEST** — applies a fixed 50% brake current for five seconds. Used to verify brake operation.
5. **FAULT LOG** — displays the last 20 fault codes with time and date stamps.
6. **CONTRAST** — adjusts the display contrast. Range: 0 to 15.

## 6.3 Installation and Wiring

### 6.3.1 Mechanical Installation

The WTC is a panel-mounted unit. It is supplied with four M4 mounting studs and a rubber gasket. The panel cut-out is 92 mm × 92 mm, to DIN 43700. The unit should be mounted in a location where the ambient temperature does not exceed 45 °C and where it is not subject to vibration in excess of 0.5 g.

The load cells are mounted on the dancer roller shaft, one at each end. The load cells are rated at 200 kg each. The cable from each load cell is screened and should be routed separately from any power cables. The screen should be earthed at the controller end only.

**Important:** Do not route the load cell cables in the same cable tray as the brake coil cable. The PWM signal on the brake cable can induce noise in the load cell cables, causing unstable tension readings.

### 6.3.2 Electrical Connections

All electrical connections are made to the terminal block on the rear of the unit. The terminal block is a 12-way plug-in connector, type WAGO 734. The connections are as follows:

| Terminal | Function | Wire Size |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | 24 V DC supply (positive) | 1.5 mm² |
| 2 | 0 V supply (negative) | 1.5 mm² |
| 3 | Load cell 1 signal (+) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 4 | Load cell 1 signal (−) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 5 | Load cell 2 signal (+) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 6 | Load cell 2 signal (−) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 7 | Brake coil positive | 2.5 mm² |
| 8 | Brake coil negative | 2.5 mm² |
| 9 | Remote stop input | 1.0 mm² |
| 10 | Remote start input | 1.0 mm² |
| 11 | Fault relay (normally open) | 1.0 mm² |
| 12 | Fault relay (common) | 1.0 mm² |

**Warning:** The 24 V DC supply must be fused at 2 A. The supply must be isolated from the main AC supply by a safety isolating transformer to EN 61558. The brake coil is a 24 V DC device with a resistance of approximately 8 Ω. The maximum brake current is 3 A.

### 6.3.3 Earth Bonding

The controller must be earthed via the earth stud on the rear panel. The earth stud is an M4 screw, and the earth cable should be at least 2.5 mm². The earth connection must be made before the machine is connected to the electrical supply.
# 7 TROUBLESHOOTING

## 7.1 Introduction

This section provides a systematic guide to diagnosing and rectifying common faults that may occur on the Marlowe & Vine press and its ancillary equipment. The procedures are arranged by symptom, with the most likely causes listed first. Always isolate the machine from the electrical supply before carrying out any work, unless the procedure specifically requires the machine to be energised for testing.

Before commencing any troubleshooting activity, ensure that you have the following to hand:

- The relevant section of this manual
- A multimeter with a DC current range
- The spare parts list for the machine (Section 12)
- The work order pad and a pen

If a fault is not covered in this section, or if the suggested remedies do not resolve the problem, contact the Marlowe & Vine technical support line. Have the machine serial number and the controller software version available when you call.

## 7.2 Web Breaks

A web break is the most common cause of unscheduled downtime on the press. The causes can be broadly divided into three categories: material defects, machine faults, and operator error. The following table lists the most frequent causes and their remedies.

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Remedy |
|---------|--------------|--------|
| Web breaks at the unwind, usually within the first 50 m of a new reel | Reel core out of round, or core damaged in transit | Inspect core before loading. Reject any reel with a damaged core. |
| Web breaks at the same point on every reel, always at the nip | Nip roll pressure too high, causing scoring of the web | Check nip pressure against Section 5.4.2. Reduce pressure and re-check. |
| Web breaks at the infeed, accompanied by a flapping sound | Infeed dancer roller out of alignment | Check dancer roller parallelism against Section 6.2.1. Re-align if necessary. |
| Web breaks at the printing unit, with ink build-up on the impression cylinder | Ink tack too high for the substrate | Reduce ink tack with a suitable reducer, or slow the press speed. |
| Web breaks at the dryer exit, web appears scorched | Dryer temperature too high, or web stalled in dryer | Check dryer temperature against Section 5.6. Check web path for obstructions. |
| Web breaks at the rewind, with the web wrapped around the rewind roller | Rewind tension too low | Increase rewind tension. See Section 6.3.5. |
| Random web breaks at the unwind, no pattern | Worn brake pads on the unwind brake | Inspect brake pads. Replace if worn beyond 2 mm thickness. |

**Note:** A web break that occurs at the same position on the web, but at different points in the machine, is usually caused by a defect in the web itself, such as a splice failure or a weak spot in the paper. A web break that occurs at the same position in the machine, but at different points on the web, is usually caused by a machine fault.

## 7.3 Tension Control Faults

The tension control system is described in Section 6.3. The following faults are those most commonly reported.

### 7.3.1 Unstable Tension at the Unwind

**Symptoms:** The tension reading on the controller display fluctuates by more than ±5% of the set point, even when the press speed is constant. The web may flutter or hunt.

**Possible causes, in order of likelihood:**

1. **Load cell cable noise.** The load cell cables are screened and must be routed separately from power cables. If the cables have been re-routed, or if a new cable has been installed, check that the screen is earthed at the controller end only. Check that the load cell cables are not in the same cable tray as the brake coil cable. The PWM signal on the brake cable can induce noise in the load cell cables, causing unstable tension readings.
## 7.3.2 Tension Reading Erratic but Web Appears Stable

**Symptoms:** The tension display shows large swings (±10% or more), but the web does not flutter and print register is unaffected. The fault may come and go over several hours.

**Possible causes, in order of likelihood:**

1. **Faulty load cell or load cell amplifier.** If the load cell reading is erratic but the web is stable, suspect the measuring system rather than the tension control loop. Check the load cell zero offset. With the web threaded and stationary, the display should read within ±2% of the mechanical zero. If not, re-zero following Section 6.3.2. If the reading drifts after re-zeroing, replace the load cell.

2. **Loose connection in the load cell cable.** Check all connectors at the load cell, the junction box (if fitted), and the controller. A loose connector will produce intermittent readings that may not affect web stability if the control loop responds slowly.

3. **Earthing problem.** A second earth path on the load cell cable screen can cause a hum that appears as a tension fluctuation. The screen must be earthed at the controller end only. Check that the screen is not also earthed at the load cell end.

4. **Controller display fault.** If the web is stable and the tension reading is wrong, the display or its driver circuit may be faulty. Compare the display reading with the value on the controller's service screen (see Section 6.3.7). If the service screen reading is stable, replace the display module.

**Note:** A tension reading that is erratic only when the dryer is running, or only when the chill roll section is running, is usually caused by electrical noise from the drive inverter. Check that the inverter output cables are screened and that the screen is earthed at the inverter end only.

### 7.3.3 Tension Drift at Constant Speed

**Symptoms:** The tension reading slowly increases or decreases over several minutes, even though the press speed is constant. The web may not show any visible change.

**Possible causes, in order of likelihood:**

1. **Brake temperature drift.** The unwind brake torque changes as the brake temperature changes. If the brake is running hot, the torque may drop as the friction material heats up. Check the brake surface temperature with a contact thermometer. If it exceeds 90 °C, check the air gap and the brake adjustment (Section 6.3.4).

2. **Load cell thermal drift.** The load cells can drift if they are exposed to heat from the dryer or from the brake. Check that the load cells are not mounted close to a heat source. If they are, fit a heat shield.

3. **Controller PID integral wind-up.** If the tension has been adjusted manually, or if the press has been stopped for a long time, the integral term may have wound up. Reset the controller to automatic, then press the "Reset" key on the controller face. See Section 6.3.8 for the reset procedure.

4. **Web splice.** A splice in the web can cause a slow tension change as the splice passes through the machine. This is normal and should not be treated as a fault unless the change is large or the splice fails.

### 7.3.4 Tension Oscillation (Hunting)

**Symptoms:** The tension reading oscillates at a regular frequency, typically between 1 and 5 seconds per cycle. The web may flutter visibly.

**Possible causes, in order of likelihood:**

1. **Controller gain too high.** The tension control loop is oscillating. Reduce the proportional gain, or increase the damping, following the tuning procedure in Section 6.3.9. If the oscillation stops when the gain is reduced, the original gain setting was too high.

2. **Dancer roller friction.** If the machine has a dancer roller, check that the dancer bearings turn freely and that the dancer is not sticking. A sticking dancer can cause the tension to oscillate even when the controller is correctly tuned. Lubricate the dancer bearings with a light machine oil (see Section 8.2, lubrication schedule).

documents.title: Marlowe & Vine Press Manual 2023
documents.content:
**1.1 Purpose**
This manual provides operating and maintenance instructions for Press No. 3, a web offset printing press manufactured for the Marlowe & Vine Group. The manual is intended for use by trained press operators, maintenance technicians, and shift supervisors. All personnel must read and understand the relevant sections before operating or servicing the press.

**1.2 Safety Warnings**
- **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Always isolate the main electrical supply and pneumatic supply before performing any maintenance or cleaning task that requires access to moving parts. Use the assigned lock and tag. Only the person who applied the lock may remove it.
- **Nip Points:** The press contains multiple in-running nips. Keep hands, loose clothing, and tools clear of all nips. Guards must be in place at all times except during approved maintenance.
- **Hot Surfaces:** Dryer and chill roll sections operate at high temperatures. Allow components to cool for at least 15 minutes after shutdown before accessing them.
- **Chemical Safety:** Blanket washes and solvents are flammable. Use only in well-ventilated areas. No smoking or open flames in the press hall. Refer to SDS sheets in the control room.
- **Noise:** Sound levels may exceed 85 dBA during operation. Wear hearing protection when in the press hall.
- **Lifting:** Use approved lifting points only. Never lift the press or its major components by hand. Use the overhead crane for units heavier than 50 kg.
- **Emergency Stop:** The press is equipped with emergency stop (E-stop) buttons at each unit and at the main control console. Pressing any E-stop will immediately halt the press drive and close the pneumatic line. Restart requires a full reset procedure (see Section 4.8).
- **Electrical Safety:** Only qualified electricians may open electrical enclosures. Capacitors may retain a charge; discharge as per Section 11.3.

**1.3 Training Requirement**
Only personnel who have completed the Marlowe & Vine Press Operator Training Program and have been signed off on Press No. 3 are authorized to operate the press. A list of authorised operators is maintained on the noticeboard outside the press hall.

---

**2. General Specifications**

**2.1 Press Configuration**
Press No. 3 is a four-unit, heat-set web offset press with a 578 mm web width and a 620 mm cut-off. It is configured for two-side printing on coated and uncoated papers. The press is fitted with an in-line folder and a sheeter.

**2.2 Speed Rating**
The manual states that Press No. 3 has press speed rating 45000 copies per hour. Record status: current. This rating is based on a standard 16-page signature (broadsheet) at a basis weight of 50 gsm. Speed is measured at the folder delivery. The press may be operated at speeds up to this rating, but running at maximum speed for extended periods may increase wear on the blanket cylinders and paper dust build-up in the folder. For running speed recommendations based on stock, refer to Section 4.4.

**2.3 Dimensional and Weight Data (Approximate)**

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Overall Length (infeed to folder) | 22.4 m |
| Overall Width (including console) | 4.8 m |
| Height to top of dryer | 3.1 m |
| Total Weight (dry) | 38,500 kg |
| Max Paper Roll Diameter | 1.25 m |
| Max Paper Roll Width | 590 mm |

**2.4 Electrical Supply**
- Main Supply: 400V, 3-phase, 50Hz
- Control Voltage: 24V DC
- Total Installed Load: 185 kW (excluding dryer)
- Dryer Load: 95 kW

**2.5 Pneumatic Supply**
- Required Pressure: 6.5 bar (max 8 bar)
- Air Quality: Filtered to 5 microns, dried to a dew point of +3°C
- Consumption: 12 m³/hr at full speed

**2.6 Water Supply (Chill Roll System)**
- Inlet Temperature: 10-12°C
- Flow Rate: 80 L/min per chill roll stand
- Water Quality: Treated, pH 7.0-8.5

**Table 3.1 – Recommended Web Tensions (N/m of web width)**

| Stock Type | Basis Weight (gsm) | Tension (N/m) |
|------------|--------------------|---------------|
| Newsprint   | 40–45             | 350           |
| Uncoated    | 50–60             | 420           |
| Coated      | 60–70             | 480           |
| Coated      | 70–80             | 520           |

These values are for a single web. If running a double-web configuration, add 15% to the total tension setting. Tension should be checked at the beginning of each shift and after any change of reel. The tension readout on the console shows the value at the infeed nip.

Note: The tension values above were revised in the 2023 update. The previous edition of this manual (2019) listed values approximately 10% lower, based on the older dancer-roll control system. The new values reflect the upgraded load-cell system installed in early 2022. If any part of the press still uses the older dancer-roll settings, refer to the archived Section 3.3 in the 2019 manual held in the maintenance office.

**3.4 Web Guides**

Two web guides are fitted: one at the infeed and one ahead of the folder. Each guide uses an infra-red edge sensor to keep the web laterally aligned. The guide rollers are pneumatically positioned.

- Guide response time: 0.2 seconds (nominal)
- Maximum lateral correction: ±15 mm
- Air supply to guides: 6.5 bar, as per Section 2.5

If a guide oscillates or fails to hold position, check the sensor lens for paper dust. Clean with a soft, dry cloth only. Do not use solvent. If the guide continues to hunt, check the air pressure at the guide manifold and the condition of the guide rollers for wear.

**3.5 Web Break Detectors**

Web break detectors are located:

- After the infeed unit
- After each printing unit
- After the chill roll stands
- At the folder inlet

According to the manual, Press No. 3 has web width 1.4 metres. Record status: current.

The detectors are contact-type, using a low-voltage sensing bar. When a break is detected, the press stops automatically and the detector location is shown on the console display. The web break detector sensitivity should be checked weekly. Adjust the sensitivity so that a light finger press on the sensing bar triggers a stop, but normal web flutter does not.

**3.6 Chill Roll Stands**

There are two chill roll stands, each with three rolls. The chill roll system is supplied with treated water at 10–12°C and a flow rate of 80 L/min per stand, as per Section 2.6. The water temperature is controlled by the chiller unit located outside the press hall.

Web tension through the chill roll stands should be maintained at the same value as the infeed tension. If the web is over-tensioned through the chill rolls, it can cause ink picking on coated stocks. If under-tensioned, the web can bag and cause wrinkles at the folder.

**3.7 Folder Infeed Tension**

The folder infeed has its own nip roll set. Tension here should be slightly lower than the main web tension – approximately 90% of the value in Table 3.1. This prevents web pull at the folder former. The folder nip pressure is set hydraulically and should be checked during the weekly preventive maintenance routine.

**3.8 Dryer**

The dryer is a hot-air, gas-fired unit. The dryer temperature profile is set by the operator according to the ink coverage and stock type. Typical settings are given in Section 4.4. The dryer has an automatic web break shutdown that isolates the gas supply if a web break occurs while the press is running.

**4. Printing Units**

**4.1 Unit Configuration**

Press No. 3 has four printing units, each configured for one colour. The units are numbered from the infeed side: Unit 1 (black), Unit 2 (cyan), Unit 3 (magenta), Unit 4 (yellow). Each unit has a blanket cylinder, plate cylinder, and impression cylinder arrangement.

documents.content:
The dryer temperature profile should be set according to the ink coverage and stock type. The following table gives typical settings. These are starting points only; the operator should adjust them based on the actual print result.

| Stock Type          | Ink Coverage | Dryer Temperature (°C) |
|---------------------|--------------|------------------------|
| Newsprint           | Light        | 90–100                 |
| Newsprint           | Heavy        | 110–120                |
| Coated stock        | Light        | 100–110                |
| Coated stock        | Heavy        | 120–130                |

If the dryer temperature is set too high, the web can blister or curl. If set too low, the ink will not dry properly and can mark or set off on the folder.

**4.5 Ink Viscosity Specifications**

The ink viscosity should be maintained within the following ranges. Viscosity is measured using the standard flow cup supplied with the press. The measurement should be taken at the unit, not at the bulk supply tank, because the viscosity can change as the ink travels through the pipework.

| Ink Colour | Viscosity Range (seconds) |
|------------|---------------------------|
| Black      | 25–30                     |
| Cyan       | 28–32                     |
| Magenta    | 28–32                     |
| Yellow     | 30–35                     |

**4.6 Plate Cylinder and Blanket Cylinder**

The plate cylinder has a single plate lockup. The plate is clamped at the leading edge and tensioned at the trailing edge. When fitting a new plate, the trailing edge should be pulled tight to prevent the plate from working loose during the run. The plate cylinder bearer rings should be checked for wear during the monthly maintenance routine. If the bearers are worn, the plate can bounce and cause a visible band across the print.

The manual lists Press No. 3 has oil filter part number MV-3456-01. Record status: current.

The blanket cylinder is fitted with a compressible blanket. The blanket should be replaced when the print quality deteriorates, typically after 500,000 impressions. The blanket should be cleaned with the automatic blanket wash system at the end of each shift. The blanket wash system uses a solvent which is supplied from the central solvent supply.

The blanket cylinder bearer rings should be checked for wear at the same time as the plate cylinder bearers. If the bearers are worn, the nip pressure will be uneven, and this can cause a ghosting effect in the print.

**4.7 Impression Cylinder**

The impression cylinder is not fitted with a blanket. The impression cylinder provides the backing for the web as it passes through the nip. The impression cylinder surface should be kept clean and free from ink build-up. If ink builds up on the impression cylinder, it can transfer to the back of the web and cause marking in the next unit.

**5. Ancillary Equipment**

**5.1 Oil Lubrication System**

Press No. 3 is fitted with a centralised oil lubrication system. The system supplies oil to the main bearings, the gearboxes, and the folders. The oil is pumped from a reservoir located in the basement below the press hall. The oil level in the reservoir should be checked daily, and the oil should be topped up if the level is below the minimum mark on the sight glass.

The oil lubrication system has a filter which should be replaced every 6 months. The filter is a spin-on type. The part number for the oil filter for Press No. 3 is MV-3456-01. This part number is current and should be used when ordering replacements. The oil filter is located on the side of the oil reservoir, and it is accessible from the walkway at the infeed end of the press. Record status: current.

documents.title: Marlowe & Vine Press Manual 2023
documents.content:
The system pressure should be maintained between 2.0 and 2.5 bar. The pressure is set by the pressure-reducing valve on the make-up water line. If the pressure drops below 1.5 bar, the low-pressure switch will stop the press. The make-up water is supplied from the mains via a float valve in the header tank. The header tank is located on the roof above the press hall.

The water filters are bag-type filters. They should be replaced when the differential pressure across the filter reaches 1.0 bar. The differential pressure is shown on the gauge on the filter housing. The part number for the water filter bags is MV-2210-BAG. Record status: current.

**5.3 Ancillary Pumps**

The press hall is served by several ancillary pumps. These pumps are used for the oil lubrication system, the water circulation system, and the solvent supply system. The pumps are not part of the main press drive.

The pumps are grouped together in the pump room, which is located at the basement level below the press hall. The pump room is accessed via the stairs at the reelstand end of the press. The pump room is also used for storage of maintenance materials. Do not store rags or solvent-soaked waste in the pump room. They must be kept in the designated fire-proof bins outside the pump room.

Each pump has a nameplate attached to the motor. The nameplate shows the pump type, the serial number, and the date of manufacture. The serial number should be quoted on all parts orders and in the maintenance log.

**5.4 Ancillary Pump 7**

Ancillary Pump 7 is located at the far end of the pump room, next to the oil reservoir. The manual specifies Ancillary Pump 7 has pump type centrifugal. Record status: current.

Ancillary Pump 7 is used for the transfer of oil from the bulk storage tank to the oil reservoir. The bulk storage tank is located outside the pump room, against the basement wall. The pump is not used for the main oil circulation loop.

The pump is a close-coupled centrifugal pump. The pump is driven by a 5.5 kW electric motor. The motor is a three-phase, 415 V, 50 Hz unit. The motor is fitted with a thermal overload relay which is set to the motor full-load current. The overload relay is located in the motor starter panel, which is mounted on the wall adjacent to the pump.

The pump discharge pressure should be checked when the pump is running. The normal discharge pressure is between 3.0 and 4.0 bar. The discharge pressure is shown on the gauge on the discharge pipework. The gauge is a glycerine-filled type. The pump suction pressure is not normally monitored. If the suction strainer becomes blocked, the pump will cavitate. Cavitation can be heard as a rattling or knocking noise from the pump.

The pump is fitted with a mechanical seal. The mechanical seal requires no routine maintenance. The seal should be inspected for leaks during the monthly visual inspection. If the seal leaks, the pump must be taken out of service and the seal replaced. The seal kit part number is MV-2210-SEAL.

**5.4.1 Ancillary Pump 7 Installation Notes**

The pump is mounted on a concrete plinth. The plinth is raised 150 mm above the pump room floor. The pump is secured to the plinth with four M16 foundation bolts. The foundation bolts are grouted into the plinth. The pump alignment should be checked after any work on the foundation bolts.

The suction pipework is 80 mm nominal bore. The discharge pipework is 50 mm nominal bore. The discharge pipework rises vertically from the pump and then runs along the wall to the oil reservoir. The discharge pipework is fitted with a non-return valve. The non-return valve is located immediately after the discharge gate valve. The discharge gate valve is used to isolate the pump for maintenance.

**5.4.2.1 Performance Curve**

The performance curve for Ancillary Pump 7 is reproduced in Drawing MV-AP7-PC-001,
which is held in the drawing register in the maintenance office. A reduced-size copy is
mounted on the wall inside the pump room, next to the motor starter panel. The curve
shows the relationship between flow and discharge head for the pump at 1450 rpm.

The curve is based on the works test and has been verified on site. Site verification
was carried out using the temporary flow meter that is kept in the stores. The
temporary flow meter is a clamp-on ultrasonic type. It is not permanently installed.
The meter is suitable for flow measurement on the 50 mm discharge pipework.

Three points from the curve are reproduced below for quick reference. These are the
points most often used when checking pump performance.

**Table 5.4.2.2 – Performance Curve Reference Points**

| Flow (L/min) | Discharge Head (m) | Equivalent Pressure (bar) | Notes |
|--------------|--------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| 60 | 34.5 | 3.4 | Low flow, high head |
| 120 | 31.0 | 3.0 | Duty point |
| 160 | 24.5 | 2.4 | High flow, low head |

The manual indicates Ancillary Pump 7 has rated flow 120 litres per minute. Record status: current.

The discharge head is measured in metres of liquid column. The equivalent pressure is
given in bar for convenience, and assumes the oil specific gravity is 0.88. If a
different oil is used, the pressure gauge reading will change even though the pump is
operating at the same point on the curve. Do not use the pressure gauge reading to
infer flow unless the oil specific gravity is known.

**5.4.2.2 Effect of Oil Viscosity**

The performance data given in Section 5.4.2.1 is for oil with a viscosity of 32 cSt at
40 °C. This is the standard oil used in the press lubrication system. If a higher
viscosity oil is used, the pump flow will be reduced at the same discharge pressure.
The motor current will also increase.

For oil with a viscosity of 46 cSt at 40 °C, the flow at the duty point is reduced by
approximately 8%. This should be taken into account when estimating reservoir fill
time. If a viscosity of 68 cSt is used, the flow reduction is approximately 15%. The
pump is not suitable for oils with a viscosity above 68 cSt without consultation with
the pump manufacturer.

The viscosity of the oil in use should be checked when investigating any apparent
reduction in pump flow. The oil viscosity is normally stated on the oil delivery
certificate. A simple check is to compare the oil temperature at the pump suction with
the expected temperature for the current operating conditions. If the oil is cooler
than normal, the viscosity will be higher and the flow will be lower.

**5.4.2.3 Flow Measurement Methods**

There is no permanently installed flow meter on the Ancillary Pump 7 discharge
pipework. Flow is inferred from the discharge pressure gauge and the performance
curve. This is sufficient for routine checks. For more accurate measurement, the
temporary flow meter can be fitted to the discharge pipework.

documents.content:
The flow meter should be installed on a straight run of pipe, with at least five
pipe diameters of straight pipe upstream and two pipe diameters downstream of the
meter. This reduces the effect of flow disturbances on the reading. For the
Ancillary Pump 7 discharge pipework, the boss is located approximately 300 mm
downstream of the pump flange, which is within an acceptable straight run.

**5.4.2.5 Pressure Gauge Check**

The discharge pressure gauge is a 0-10 bar gauge with a 63 mm dial. The gauge is
wetted with glycerine to damp vibration. Check the gauge glass for cracks or
clouding at each routine inspection. A cloudy glass can make the reading difficult
to see and should be replaced.

The gauge should read zero when the pump is stopped and the discharge valve is
closed. If the gauge does not return to zero, the gauge is faulty or the pressure
sensing line is blocked. The pressure sensing line is a 6 mm OD stainless steel
tube. It should be purged if there is any doubt about the reading. Do not rely on
a faulty gauge reading to set the pump duty point.

**5.4.3 Ancillary Pump 7 – Maintenance Schedule**

Ancillary Pump 7 is subject to a scheduled maintenance programme. The schedule is
based on operating hours, which are recorded on the pump hour meter. The hour
meter is located on the pump control panel, next to the start/stop buttons. The
reading should be recorded at the end of each shift in the Press Room Shift Log.

The manual states Ancillary Pump 7 has maintenance interval 500 operating hours. Record status: current.
This interval is current for all maintenance tasks listed in Table 5.4.3.1. The
interval is measured in operating hours, not calendar time. A pump that runs
continuously will require maintenance more frequently than a pump that runs
intermittently. Record the hour meter reading at each maintenance event and
calculate the next due date based on the expected running hours per week.

**Table 5.4.3.1 – Ancillary Pump 7 Maintenance Tasks**

| Item | Task Description | Interval (hours) | Notes |
|------|------------------|------------------|-------|
| 1 | Check oil level in bearing housing | 500 | Top up with ISO VG 32 if required |
| 2 | Check coupling alignment | 500 | Use dial indicator; max 0.1 mm |
| 3 | Check coupling element for wear | 500 | Replace if cracks or missing rubber |
| 4 | Check mechanical seal for leakage | 500 | Minor weep is acceptable; drip must be investigated |
| 5 | Check suction strainer for debris | 500 | Clean if pressure drop exceeds 0.3 bar |
| 6 | Check discharge pressure at duty point | 500 | Compare with Section 5.4.2.1 |
| 7 | Check motor current at duty point | 500 | Compare with nameplate FLA |
| 8 | Check pump vibration | 500 | Use handheld vibrometer; max 4.5 mm/s RMS |
| 9 | Check bearing temperature | 500 | Max 80 °C at bearing housing |
| 10 | Check for unusual noise | 500 | Report any change in tone or level |
| 11 | Check all pipework joints for leaks | 500 | Tighten or remake as required |
| 12 | Check baseplate bolts for tightness | 500 | Torque to 80 Nm |

The maintenance tasks listed in Table 5.4.3.1 are to be carried out at each
500 operating hour interval. The tasks should be completed by a competent
maintenance technician. After completion, the technician should sign and date the
Maintenance Record Sheet (Form MV-214) and enter the hour meter reading in the
appropriate column.

**5.4.3.1 Oil Change**

The oil in the bearing housing should be changed at every second maintenance
interval, i.e. at 1000 operating hours. The oil specification is ISO VG 32 mineral
oil. Drain the oil while the pump is warm, but not running. Remove the drain plug
at the bottom of the bearing housing and allow the oil to drain into a suitable
container. Dispose of the used oil in accordance with site procedures. Refit the
drain plug and fill with new oil to the level indicated on the sight glass. The
oil level should be at the centre of the sight glass when the pump is stopped.

**5.5 Backup Generator Set B**

Backup Generator Set B (BGS-B) provides standby electrical power to the press line
and ancillary equipment in the event of a mains supply failure. This section covers
the routine maintenance and operational checks for BGS-B. The generator is located in
the external generator compound adjacent to the press hall.

**5.5.1 General Description**

BGS-B is a diesel engine driven generator set. The engine is a six cylinder,
turbocharged diesel engine. The generator is a brushless alternator. The set is
mounted on a skid base with anti-vibration mounts. The generator set is designed for
standby duty and is not intended for continuous operation.

**5.5.2 Fuel System**

The fuel system consists of a day tank, a transfer pump, a fuel filter, and the
engine fuel injection system. The day tank is mounted on the skid base. Fuel is
supplied to the day tank from the main bulk fuel storage tank by the transfer pump.
The transfer pump is controlled by a level switch in the day tank. The fuel filter
should be changed at the intervals given in the maintenance schedule.

**5.5.2.1 Fuel Capacity**

The manual notes Backup Generator Set B has fuel capacity 800 litres. Record status: current. This is the
capacity of the day tank. The day tank is calibrated and a sight glass is fitted to
indicate the fuel level. The fuel level should be checked before each test run and
after any period of operation. If the fuel level is low, the day tank should be
topped up from the bulk storage tank using the transfer pump. The transfer pump
should be operated manually only when the generator is shut down.

**5.5.2.2 Fuel Quality**

The fuel used in BGS-B should be diesel fuel meeting the requirements of BS EN 590.
The fuel should be clean and free from water and sediment. Water in the fuel can
cause damage to the injection system. The fuel filter has a water separator element.
The water separator bowl should be drained at each maintenance interval. If the fuel
is suspected of being contaminated, a sample should be taken and tested. The bulk
fuel storage tank should be checked for water at regular intervals.

**5.5.3 Cooling System**

The engine is cooled by a radiator and fan. The cooling system is filled with a
mixture of water and antifreeze. The antifreeze concentration should be checked
before the winter period and adjusted to give protection to -20 °C. The coolant
level should be checked at each maintenance interval. The radiator fins should be
checked for blockage and cleaned with compressed air if necessary.

**5.5.4 Electrical System**

The generator set is controlled by an automatic mains failure (AMF) control panel.
The panel monitors the mains supply and initiates a start sequence for the generator
when a mains failure is detected. The panel also monitors the generator output and
provides protection against overload, short circuit, and low oil pressure. The
control panel is located in a weatherproof enclosure on the skid base.

**5.5.4.1 Control Panel Checks**

The following checks should be carried out on the control panel at each maintenance
interval:

1.  Check the panel for signs of moisture ingress or condensation.
2.  Check all indicator lamps and the digital display for correct operation.
3.  Check the battery charger for correct output voltage.
4.  Check the battery condition and electrolyte level.
5.  Check the emergency stop button for correct operation. Do not test the emergency
    stop with the generator running unless the procedure in Section 5.5.6 is being
    followed.

# 6. CONTROL SYSTEMS

## 6.1 Web Tension Controller (WTC)

The Web Tension Controller (WTC) is fitted to the main reel stand and provides closed-loop control of web tension between the unwind and the first printing unit. The controller maintains a set tension by adjusting the brake torque on the unwind shaft in response to signals from the load cells mounted on the dancer roller assembly.

The WTC is a microprocessor-based unit housed in a sheet-steel enclosure mounted on the side frame of the reel stand. The front panel comprises a backlit LCD display, a keypad for data entry, and indicator lamps for power, fault, and brake status. All operator adjustments are made via the keypad; no internal potentiometer adjustments are required for normal operation.

### 6.1.1 Technical Specifications

| Parameter | Specification |
|---|---|
| Supply voltage | 24 V DC nominal (20–30 V DC) |
| Power consumption | 12 W maximum |
| Display | 2-line × 16-character backlit LCD |
| Load cell input | 2 × 2 mV/V, 350 Ω bridge |
| Brake output | 0–24 V DC PWM, 3 A maximum |
| Analogue outputs | 0–10 V DC, 4–20 mA (isolated) |
| Serial interface | RS-485, Modbus RTU |
| Operating temperature | 0–50 °C |
| Enclosure rating | IP54 |

### 6.1.2 Firmware

The WTC is supplied with firmware version 3.2.1. The manual records Web Tension Controller has firmware version 3.2.1. Record status: current. This is the current production version and supersedes all earlier versions. The firmware version is shown on the display for approximately 5 seconds when power is applied to the unit.

Do not attempt to update the firmware in the field. Firmware updates are carried out by the manufacturer or by authorised service personnel only. The update procedure requires the use of a proprietary programming lead, which is not supplied with the machine. If the firmware version is not as stated above, contact Marlowe & Vine Group Service Department before placing the machine back into service.

### 6.1.3 Functional Description

The WTC receives signals from the two load cells mounted on the dancer roller. The load cells produce a small voltage proportional to the force applied by the web. The controller sums the two signals and compares the result with the set tension value entered by the operator. The difference between the actual and set tension produces an error signal, which is used to adjust the brake current.

The brake is a permanent-magnet particle brake. The controller supplies a pulse-width-modulated voltage to the brake coil. The duty cycle of the PWM signal determines the brake torque. The controller also provides a soft-start function to prevent web breakage on start-up.

The WTC has the following operating modes:

1. **Manual mode** — the operator sets the brake current directly as a percentage of full scale. The load cell feedback is ignored. This mode is used for initial set-up and for troubleshooting.
2. **Automatic mode** — the controller maintains the set tension using load cell feedback. This is the normal operating mode.
3. **Calibration mode** — used to zero the load cells and to set the full-scale calibration. Access to this mode requires a four-digit code, which is given in Section 6.1.6.

## 6.2 WTC Operator Controls

### 6.2.1 Front Panel

The front panel is arranged as follows:

- **Power lamp** — illuminated when 24 V DC is present.
- **Fault lamp** — illuminated when a fault condition is detected. The display shows the fault code (see Section 6.4).
- **Brake lamp** — illuminated when the brake is being energised.
- **Display** — two lines of 16 characters. Shows tension in kg, brake current as a percentage, and fault codes.
- **Keypad** — six keys: UP, DOWN, ENTER, ESC, MAN/AUTO, and CAL.

documents.title: Marlowe & Vine Press Manual 2023
documents.content:
### 6.2.2 Keypad Functions

The six keys on the front panel have the following functions:

| Key | Function |
|------|-----------|
| UP / DOWN | Scroll through menu items, adjust values, and select fault code display. |
| ENTER | Confirm a selection or store a value. |
| ESC | Return to the previous menu level without storing changes. |
| MAN/AUTO | Toggle between Manual and Automatic mode. When the machine is running, the mode change takes effect immediately. |
| CAL | Enter Calibration mode. This key is only active when the machine is in Manual mode and the four-digit access code has been entered. |

**Note:** The MAN/AUTO key is ignored when the web is in motion. The controller will not accept a mode change while the press is running at speeds above 50 m/min. If the operator attempts to change mode at speed, the key press is ignored and the display shows `MODE LOCKED` for three seconds.

### 6.2.3 Menu Structure

The WTC has a two-level menu structure. The top level is selected by pressing the UP or DOWN keys when the display shows the running values. The second level is entered by pressing ENTER.

The menu items are as follows:

1. **SET TENSION** — sets the target tension in kg. Range: 0.0 to 50.0 kg.
2. **CAL ZERO** — zeroes the load cell output. See Section 6.1.6.
3. **CAL SPAN** — sets the full-scale calibration. See Section 6.1.6.
4. **BRAKE TEST** — applies a fixed 50% brake current for five seconds. Used to verify brake operation.
5. **FAULT LOG** — displays the last 20 fault codes with time and date stamps.
6. **CONTRAST** — adjusts the display contrast. Range: 0 to 15.

## 6.3 Installation and Wiring

### 6.3.1 Mechanical Installation

The WTC is a panel-mounted unit. It is supplied with four M4 mounting studs and a rubber gasket. The panel cut-out is 92 mm × 92 mm, to DIN 43700. The unit should be mounted in a location where the ambient temperature does not exceed 45 °C and where it is not subject to vibration in excess of 0.5 g.

The load cells are mounted on the dancer roller shaft, one at each end. The load cells are rated at 200 kg each. The cable from each load cell is screened and should be routed separately from any power cables. The screen should be earthed at the controller end only.

**Important:** Do not route the load cell cables in the same cable tray as the brake coil cable. The PWM signal on the brake cable can induce noise in the load cell cables, causing unstable tension readings.

### 6.3.2 Electrical Connections

All electrical connections are made to the terminal block on the rear of the unit. The terminal block is a 12-way plug-in connector, type WAGO 734. The connections are as follows:

| Terminal | Function | Wire Size |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | 24 V DC supply (positive) | 1.5 mm² |
| 2 | 0 V supply (negative) | 1.5 mm² |
| 3 | Load cell 1 signal (+) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 4 | Load cell 1 signal (−) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 5 | Load cell 2 signal (+) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 6 | Load cell 2 signal (−) | 0.5 mm² screened |
| 7 | Brake coil positive | 2.5 mm² |
| 8 | Brake coil negative | 2.5 mm² |
| 9 | Remote stop input | 1.0 mm² |
| 10 | Remote start input | 1.0 mm² |
| 11 | Fault relay (normally open) | 1.0 mm² |
| 12 | Fault relay (common) | 1.0 mm² |

**Warning:** The 24 V DC supply must be fused at 2 A. The supply must be isolated from the main AC supply by a safety isolating transformer to EN 61558. The brake coil is a 24 V DC device with a resistance of approximately 8 Ω. The maximum brake current is 3 A.

### 6.3.3 Earth Bonding

The controller must be earthed via the earth stud on the rear panel. The earth stud is an M4 screw, and the earth cable should be at least 2.5 mm². The earth connection must be made before the machine is connected to the electrical supply.
